title: Final velocities after collision
description: Essential: Student must correctly state that after the first A-C collision, v_A = -1 m/s and v_C = 1 m/s.

title: Time interval between collisions
description: Essential: Student must correctly state that the time between the first and second A-C collisions is 2 s.

title: Momentum conservation in A-C collision
description: Important: Student must apply momentum conservation (m*v₁ = m*v_A + 3m*v_C) for the perfectly elastic A-C collision.

title: Energy conservation in A-C collision
description: Important: Student must apply kinetic energy conservation (½m*v₁² = ½m*v_A² + ½*3m*v_C²) for the perfectly elastic collision.

title: Common velocity of A and B
description: Important: Student must first find the common velocity v₁ = 2 m/s of A and B before the first A-C collision using momentum conservation on A and B.

title: C's stopping kinematics
description: Important: Student must calculate C's stopping time (t_C = v_C/(μ₂g) = 2 s) and displacement (x_C = v_C²/(2μ₂g) = 1 m) after the first collision.

title: A's return motion
description: Optional: Student may analyze A's motion after collision, including its deceleration due to friction with B and eventual common velocity v₂ = 1 m/s with B.

title: Sign error in velocities
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly assigns signs to post-collision velocities (e.g., v_A positive, v_C negative) or misinterprets direction.

title: Friction coefficient confusion
description: Pitfall: Student uses wrong friction coefficient (μ₁ instead of μ₂ for C's motion, or vice versa) in kinematic calculations.
